dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL with MPFR (GNU Multiple Precision Floating-Point) library calls; uses *> comments, BINARY-LONG, USAGE POINTER, EXIT PERFORM CYCLE, and z-string literals — all GnuCOBOL extensions
evidence: mpfr_padding pic x(32) suggesting MPFR struct layout

purpose.domain_detail: Expression evaluator / calculator engine; arithmetic evaluation of a token list (post-parenthesis-removal) using MPFR arbitrary-precision arithmetic
purpose.summary: This subprogram evaluates a flat token list representing a mathematical expression (after parentheses have been resolved). It processes operators in precedence order: exponentiation first, then multiplication/division, then addition/subtraction, calling MPFR library functions for arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Results and error messages are returned via linkage section parameters.

notable_features: USAGE POINTER for MPFR number handles
z-string literals for C-style null-terminated strings
CALL to external MPFR library functions (mpfr_pow, mpfr_mul, mpfr_div, mpfr_add, mpfr_sub, mpfr_cmp_si)
Operator-precedence parsing via multiple PERFORM loops
LINKAGE SECTION with complex token list structure
verdict.notes: The program is clearly a subprogram in a larger calculator/expression-parser project. The use of MPFR (GNU Multiple Precision Floating-Point Reliable Library) via CALL and the z-string literals strongly indicate GnuCOBOL. The mpfr_padding field (32 bytes) is used to match the MPFR struct size in memory. No SQL or CICS. Fixed format with some lines exceeding column 72 (GnuCOBOL tolerates this).
